Computer Security Incident Response Team - Finance (CSIRT-Fin) under CERT-In has designated the threat actor responsible for this campaign as "CRAFTY FALCON": an AI-assisted financial threat actor that surveys its targets with machine intelligence, operates at machine speed and strikes by invoking the victim's own payment and disbursement APIs. Application codebases reverse-engineered by the threat actor to develop tailored exploits; unauthorized API calls subsequently initiated using altered/modified application packages, defeating controls that assumed only the legitimate client application would call the APIs. IP allow-listing bypassed by originating traffic from whitelisted third-party fetcher IP pools (such as content-acceleration and app-store review fetchers); any Internet user can cause such shared fetcher services to fetch arbitrary URLs. Micro-value test transactions (such as Rs. 1) performed to validate unauthorized fund flows before executing large-value transfers. Merchant settlement APIs of payment aggregators exploited or abused to move funds. Newly published vulnerabilities exploited as soon as they become public, including file-upload and deserialization exploit chains leading to web shells in PHP and Node.js applications. Cryptocurrency exchanges and virtual digital asset service providers targeted, with wallet keys stolen and funds siphoned from cryptocurrency wallets. Large numbers of custom, tailored scripts created on the fly, with functionally identical variants refined in rapid succession; a pattern consistent with AI-generated code and iterative AI-assisted development. Recommended Actions Treat this campaign as active and escalating: maintain heightened 24x7 security monitoring, with increased staffing and lowered alert thresholds during holidays, weekends and other low-coverage windows. After any incident, assume persistence: perform full eradication with forensic verification and continue periodic threat hunting; entities have been re-attacked after incomplete remediation. Enable centralized, real-time monitoring of cloud audit logs with alerting on high-risk events such as remote command execution, serverless function code updates and creation of roles, users or access keys. Enforce instance metadata service protections and least-privilege roles for instances and functions; deny wildcard egress in security groups; configure serverless functions with no Internet egress by default. Alert on token usage from unusual source IPs, user agents or geographies; enforce branch protection, commit signing and mandatory code review on production deployment branches. Replace IP allow-listing of shared third-party fetcher pools with identity-based controls such as mutual TLS, cryptographically signed requests or scoped API keys on dedicated vendor endpoints. Enforce default-deny egress from server segments through allow-listed proxies; unrestricted HTTPS egress was used for command-and-control and data exfiltration.
